Redox reactions are important, really really important. Understanding and being able to balance out redox reactions gives you insight into a huge range of phenomena. The crazy thing is that it's chemistry 301 type stuff and at least at my university the professor had 0 interest in teaching it and made it the most boring thing possible. A common little mnemonic to help you: OILRIG: Oxidation is loss. Reduction is gain.

As an example of their utility, the creation of methane rocket fuel on Mars from local carbon dioxide, the Sabatier Reaction, is a redox reaction. Another example is the chemical process that results when CO2 is absorbed by our oceans and how this ultimately ends up generating hydrogen ions resulting in an acidification of the ocean.
